newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro to have 12,000 mobile phones in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro to have 12,000 mobile phones in 1998.

text.p: Montenegro's mobile telephone company ProMonte GSM said the number of mobile phones in Montenegro will grow to 12,000 next year from the present 8,500, state news agency Tanjug reported on Wednesday.

Mobile telephones now cover around 80 percent of populated territory of Montenegro and ProMonte plans to expand the network to practically the entire republic by 2000, ProMonte director for Montenegro Sven Martin Pedersen was quoted as saying.

ProMonte will add a roaming link this month which will enable subscribers in Montenegro to use their mobile phones on the territory of Serbia, Norway, Italy, Greece, Macedonia and Switzerland, company officials told a news conference in Podgorica.
The company said around 22 million German marks had been invested in the mobile phone project in Montenegro and another six million marks would to be invested by the end of the year.

The Podgorica-based joint venture was formed in July 1996 by Montenegrin post and telecommunications company PTT Crne Gore and a Greek-Norwegian consortium, including Norway's Telenor, which owns a majority stake in the company.

Serbia, which together with Montenegro makes up the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, has two GSM mobile phone operators, Mobtel and Telekom Srbija, which sold a 49 percent stake to OTE of Greece and Stet of Italy last month.
Montenegro accounts for some 600,000 of Yugoslavia's total population of 11 million. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
